Task: Implement declarative strategy triggers and deterministic due scheduler
Description: Build declarative strategy trigger types in mike_trade/scheduling/triggers.py and one engine-owned scheduler in mike_trade/scheduling/scheduler.py. Put the unit tests in tests/unit/test_scheduler_triggers.py.

Required behavior:
- Trigger declarations are frozen value objects. Strategies attach them to their BUY or SELL class through configuration. Supported kinds:
  - MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL (any new trade or bar for the symbol)
  - QUOTE_CHANGE (bid or ask actually changed)
  - CANDLE_CLOSED(timeframe), for 1m, 5m, 15m and any other configured timeframe the h.1 candle builders support
  - INTERVAL(seconds)
  - SESSION_OPEN
  - ENTRY_CUTOFF
  - SESSION_CLOSE
  - MANUAL
  Trigger declarations are validated at load time. A positive interval and a supported timeframe are required. An unknown kind raises a typed configuration error.
- The scheduler is a single asyncio-driven component owned by the engine. It is not a thread or task per symbol or per strategy. It keeps a registry of (symbol, strategy_id, side, trigger set) for roughly 1-10 watched symbols and every enabled strategy.
- Inputs are scheduling events:
  - market-data arrival or quote change carrying a snapshot version
  - candle-closed carrying (symbol, timeframe, bar end UTC)
  - session events from the h.3 calendar (open, entry cutoff, close)
  - control ticks from an injected clock
  - manual evaluation requests
- Output is an ordered list of immutable DueEvaluation records: symbol, strategy_id, side, trigger kind, snapshot_version, bar key, due_at UTC.
- A global control cadence is only an upper tick. A control tick must not make CANDLE_CLOSED or other closed-bar strategies re-evaluate when their (symbol, timeframe, last closed bar end, snapshot_version) watermark is unchanged. INTERVAL triggers fire at most once per elapsed interval, measured with the injected clock.
- Duplicate suppression: the same (strategy_id, side, symbol, trigger kind, bar key or snapshot_version) never yields more than one DueEvaluation.
- Ordering is deterministic for identical inputs. Sort by:
  1. due_at
  2. trigger priority: session events, then candle close, then quote/data, then interval, then manual
  3. symbol
  4. strategy_id
  5. side
- All times are timezone-aware UTC. Session boundaries come from the existing exchange calendar in America/New_York. Do not hardcode wall-clock hours.
- Paused strategies, disabled strategies and unwatched symbols produce no DueEvaluation. MANUAL still produces one only when explicitly requested for an enabled strategy and watched symbol.
- The scheduler never evaluates strategies, calls brokers, opens data connections, or submits orders. It only decides what is due.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/scheduling/calendar.py (h.3) for session open, entry cutoff and close
- mike_trade/market_data/candles.py (h.1) for timeframe and closed-bar types
- mike_trade/market_data/context.py (h.4) for snapshot version semantics
- mike_trade/strategies/base.py, mike_trade/strategies/registry.py and mike_trade/domain/strategy_types.py (if present) for strategy identity and side types
- any existing clock port under mike_trade/ports/ or mike_trade/domain/ (if present)
Phase: I
Acceptance criteria:
  - A test constructs each supported trigger kind (MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL, QUOTE_CHANGE, CANDLE_CLOSED for 1m/5m/15m, INTERVAL, SESSION_OPEN, ENTRY_CUTOFF, SESSION_CLOSE, MANUAL) and confirms it is frozen. Negative tests confirm that a non-positive interval, an unsupported timeframe and an unknown kind each raise a typed configuration error.
  - A test confirms that a CANDLE_CLOSED(1m) strategy yields exactly one DueEvaluation per newly closed bar. Repeated control ticks with an unchanged closed-bar watermark yield zero additional evaluations.
  - A test confirms that an INTERVAL(30s) trigger fires at most once per elapsed 30 seconds under an injected fake clock, regardless of how many control ticks occur.
  - A test confirms that QUOTE_CHANGE fires only when bid or ask actually changes. An identical repeated quote yields nothing.
  - A test confirms that SESSION_OPEN, ENTRY_CUTOFF and SESSION_CLOSE fire once per session at the times the injected calendar reports, including an early-close session.
  - A test feeds the same event sequence twice, including simultaneous events across several symbols and strategies, and confirms identical DueEvaluation output order both times, matching the documented sort key.
  - Tests confirm that disabled or paused strategies and unwatched symbols produce no DueEvaluation, and that MANUAL produces one only on explicit request.
  - A test or code-level assertion confirms the scheduler does not create a thread or asyncio task per symbol or per strategy. Registering 10 symbols with several strategies leaves the live task/thread count unchanged.
  - The scheduler modules import no broker or provider adapter, and tests run only with injected fakes and a fake clock.

# AGENTS.md

## Purpose

This repository is operated by an autonomous multi-agent system (abracapocus_2).
All agents must follow these rules when modifying the codebase.

---

## Core Principles

- Minimal blast radius: only modify what is required for the task
- Deterministic verification: all changes must be verifiable via code (tests, compile, scripts)
- No architecture drift: do not introduce new frameworks or major design changes unless explicitly required
- No unrelated refactors
- All changes must be reproducible from a clean clone

---

## Project Structure

- docs/ → design, plans, architecture constraints
- plans/ → master plans
- phases/ → phase definitions
- tasks/ → executable task documents
- backends/ → CLI backend adapters
- agents/ → specialist agents
- runtime/ → orchestration, routing, state
- reports/ → execution reports (DO NOT MODIFY MANUALLY)
- state/runtime_state.json → runtime state (DO NOT COMMIT)

---

## Task Execution Rules

- Always operate from a task document when available
- Respect:
  - selected_backend
  - verification_profile
  - acceptance_criteria
- If a task conflicts with architecture constraints or phase scope:
  - STOP and report conflict

---

## Backend Rules

- Backends must:
  - execute commands deterministically
  - capture stdout, stderr, exit_code
  - not silently fail
- Do not invent backend interfaces; use existing adapters
- Codex CLI, Aider, Gemini, Claude Code should be invoked through backends only

---

## Verification Rules

- Verification must be deterministic
- Preferred checks:
  - pytest
  - python -m py_compile
- Do not rely on model self-evaluation

---

## Execution Control Flow (PERMANENT ARCHITECTURAL RULE)

**HEURISTIC INFERENCE MUST NEVER PARTICIPATE IN ABRACAPOCUS EXECUTION CONTROL FLOW.**

Abracapocus must not determine execution success, failure, acceptance,
rejection, blocking, retry eligibility, phase progression, or completion from
heuristic inference. A heuristic is any conclusion that is *inferred* rather
than *directly established by an explicit executable contract or a concrete
runtime fact*.

Runtime status is derived ONLY from concrete, mechanically observable facts:

1. The backend process exit code. A backend that exits `0` (with no hard
   write-policy violation) is a successful execution.
2. Objectively observed hard write-policy violations (changed paths outside the
   declared allowed write paths).
3. Explicit operator-authored commands (task/phase verification the plan
   explicitly contains). Their raw results are reported, kept DISTINCT from
   backend execution status.
4. Objective orchestrator failures with direct evidence (backend could not
   launch, required document could not be parsed, subprocess infrastructure
   failed).

**Verification results are observational and must not rewrite backend execution
status.** A verifier returning non-zero must NEVER, by itself, turn a
successful backend execution into unverified, stop a phase, or trigger an
automatic rerun. Verification is the result of a command, not authority to
rewrite history.

**Execution control:** Task-local problems (non-zero exit, timeout,
write-policy violation, frame failure, backend launch failure) produce
acceptance status ``"unverified"`` with truthful evidence preserved. They
MUST NOT stop sibling tasks, later phases, or the plan. Only operator
cancellation (SIGINT/SIGTERM/dashboard cancel) may terminate a run
(acceptance status ``"interrupted"``). Dependencies are ordering constraints,
not acceptance gates — any terminal attempt outcome satisfies a dependency
edge. The status ``"failed"`` is banned from acceptance output.

Do NOT reintroduce -- under any name, feature flag, "advisory" wrapper, or
compatibility mode -- context completeness/sufficiency scoring, change or
architecture assessment used as a gate, intent/scope matching, reconciliation
gates, no-progress judgments, confidence/risk scores, model/LLM/reviewer
judgments over status, shadow/adaptive/secondary-verification gates, or
heuristic retry/failure-classification control flow. Failure classification may
only *summarize* an already-established concrete failure; it must never create
one. Retries are permitted only for explicitly defined mechanical backend
failures. Future agents must not add these systems back.

---

## Git Rules

- Do not commit:
  - runtime_state.json
  - reports/
  - logs/
  - virtual environments
- Do not modify .gitignore unless required by task
- Do not create excessive commits; prefer grouped logical commits

---

## Allowed Changes

- Implement task requirements
- Fix failing verification
- Update relevant tests
- Improve documentation tied to the task

---

## Forbidden Changes

- Changing architecture without explicit instruction
- Adding dependencies without justification
- Modifying unrelated files
- Deleting important files
- Bypassing verification

---

## Planning Rules

- Plans are multi-phase
- Completed sections are immutable
- Remaining sections may be updated
- Tasks must align with:
  - project brief
  - architecture constraints
  - active phase

---

## Reporting

- All executions must produce structured reports
- Reports must include:
  - changed files
  - verification results
  - assessment

---

## Behavior

- Do not ask unnecessary questions
- Do not stall execution
- Do not perform broad scans unless required
- Prefer direct action over analysis

---

## Priority Order

This ordering guides *implementation decisions* only. It does NOT make
verification an acceptance authority: verification results are observational
(see "Execution Control Flow"), and never override a concrete backend
execution result.

1. Architecture constraints
2. Task definition
3. Verification results (observational signal, not acceptance authority)
4. Plan guidance

If conflicts occur, follow this order.

"""Deterministic NYSE session calendar.

The calendar is rule based and intentionally performs no I/O. Session dates are
interpreted in New York time; all public instant values are returned in UTC.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, time, timedelta
from enum import Enum
from types import MappingProxyType
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

NEW_YORK = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
SUPPORTED_YEAR_START = 2000
SUPPORTED_YEAR_END = 2035


class SessionStatus(str, Enum):
    PRE_OPEN = "PRE_OPEN"
    REGULAR = "REGULAR"
    CLOSED = "CLOSED"
    HOLIDAY = "HOLIDAY"
    UNKNOWN = "UNKNOWN"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Session:
    """An immutable regular NYSE session, including its effective close."""

    session_id: str
    session_date: date
    open_et: datetime
    close_et: datetime
    is_early_close: bool
    open_utc: datetime
    close_utc: datetime


# Override entries augment the published rule calendar.  Values are either
# ``"closed"`` or an early close time expressed as an ET wall-clock time.
SPECIAL_OVERRIDES: MappingProxyType[date, str | time] = MappingProxyType(
    {
        date(2025, 1, 9): "closed",  # National day of mourning for President Carter.
    }
)


def _check_year(day: date) -> None:
    if not SUPPORTED_YEAR_START <= day.year <= SUPPORTED_YEAR_END:
        raise ValueError(
            f"date year {day.year} is outside supported range "
            f"{SUPPORTED_YEAR_START}-{SUPPORTED_YEAR_END}"
        )


def _observed_fixed(day: date, *, new_year: bool = False) -> date | None:
    """Return a fixed-date holiday's observed date under NYSE rules."""
    if day.weekday() == 5:
        return None if new_year else day - timedelta(days=1)
    if day.weekday() == 6:
        return day + timedelta(days=1)
    return day


def _easter_sunday(year: int) -> date:
    """Gregorian Easter computus (Meeus/Jones/Butcher)."""
    a = year % 19
    b, c = divmod(year, 100)
    d, e = divmod(b, 4)
    f = (b + 8) // 25
    g = (b - f + 1) // 3
    h = (19 * a + b - d - g + 15) % 30
    i, k = divmod(c, 4)
    l = (32 + 2 * e + 2 * i - h - k) % 7
    m = (a + 11 * h + 22 * l) // 451
    month, day_num = divmod(h + l - 7 * m + 114, 31)
    return date(year, month, day_num + 1)


def _nth_weekday(year: int, month: int, weekday: int, n: int) -> date:
    first = date(year, month, 1)
    return first + timedelta(days=(weekday - first.weekday()) % 7 + 7 * (n - 1))


def _last_weekday(year: int, month: int, weekday: int) -> date:
    last_day = date(year + (month == 12), month % 12 + 1, 1) - timedelta(days=1)
    return last_day - timedelta(days=(last_day.weekday() - weekday) % 7)


def _holidays(year: int) -> frozenset[date]:
    holidays: set[date] = {
        _nth_weekday(year, 1, 0, 3),  # Martin Luther King Jr. Day
        _nth_weekday(year, 2, 0, 3),  # Washington's Birthday
        _last_weekday(year, 5, 0),  # Memorial Day
        _easter_sunday(year) - timedelta(days=2),  # Good Friday
        _nth_weekday(year, 9, 0, 1),  # Labor Day
        _nth_weekday(year, 11, 3, 4),  # Thanksgiving
    }
    for month, day_num, is_new_year in (
        (1, 1, True),
        (7, 4, False),
        (12, 25, False),
    ):
        observed = _observed_fixed(date(year, month, day_num), new_year=is_new_year)
        if observed is not None:
            holidays.add(observed)
    if year >= 2022:
        observed = _observed_fixed(date(year, 6, 19))
        if observed is not None:
            holidays.add(observed)
    return frozenset(holidays)


def _is_trading_day_unchecked(day: date) -> bool:
    if day.weekday() >= 5:
        return False
    if day in _holidays(day.year):
        return False
    return SPECIAL_OVERRIDES.get(day) != "closed"


def is_trading_day(day: date) -> bool:
    """Return whether *day* has a regular NYSE session; unknown years raise."""
    if not isinstance(day, date) or isinstance(day, datetime):
        raise TypeError("day must be a datetime.date")
    _check_year(day)
    return _is_trading_day_unchecked(day)


def session_for(day: date) -> Session:
    """Return the regular session for a trading date."""
    if not is_trading_day(day):
        raise ValueError(f"{day.isoformat()} is not a trading day")
    close_time = time(16, 0)
    early = False
    override = SPECIAL_OVERRIDES.get(day)
    if isinstance(override, time):
        close_time, early = override, True
    else:
        thanksgiving = _nth_weekday(day.year, 11, 3, 4)
        july_fourth = date(day.year, 7, 4)
        if day == thanksgiving + timedelta(days=1):
            close_time, early = time(13, 0), True
        elif day == date(day.year, 12, 24):
            close_time, early = time(13, 0), True
        elif (
            day == date(day.year, 7, 3)
            and july_fourth.weekday() in (1, 2, 3, 4)
        ):
            close_time, early = time(13, 0), True
    open_et = datetime.combine(day, time(9, 30), NEW_YORK)
    close_et = datetime.combine(day, close_time, NEW_YORK)
    return Session(
        session_id=f"XNYS-{day.isoformat()}",
        session_date=day,
        open_et=open_et,
        close_et=close_et,
        is_early_close=early,
        open_utc=open_et.astimezone(UTC),
        close_utc=close_et.astimezone(UTC),
    )


def _normalize_utc(at: datetime) -> datetime:
    if not isinstance(at, datetime) or at.tzinfo is None or at.utcoffset() is None:
        raise ValueError("at_utc must be a timezone-aware datetime")
    return at.astimezone(UTC)


def session_status(at_utc: datetime) -> SessionStatus:
    """Classify an instant; out-of-range dates are always UNKNOWN."""
    instant = _normalize_utc(at_utc)
    local_day = instant.astimezone(NEW_YORK).date()
    if not SUPPORTED_YEAR_START <= local_day.year <= SUPPORTED_YEAR_END:
        return SessionStatus.UNKNOWN
    if not _is_trading_day_unchecked(local_day):
        return SessionStatus.HOLIDAY if local_day.weekday() < 5 else SessionStatus.CLOSED
    session = session_for(local_day)
    if instant < session.open_utc:
        return SessionStatus.PRE_OPEN
    if instant < session.close_utc:
        return SessionStatus.REGULAR
    return SessionStatus.CLOSED


def is_regular_hours(at_utc: datetime) -> bool:
    return session_status(at_utc) is SessionStatus.REGULAR


def entry_cutoff(session: Session, minutes_before_close: int) -> datetime:
    """Return the UTC instant at which new entries stop for this session."""
    if not isinstance(session, Session):
        raise TypeError("session must be a Session")
    if isinstance(minutes_before_close, bool) or not isinstance(minutes_before_close, int):
        raise TypeError("minutes_before_close must be an integer")
    if minutes_before_close < 0:
        raise ValueError("minutes_before_close must be non-negative")
    return session.close_utc - timedelta(minutes=minutes_before_close)


def entries_allowed_by_time(at_utc: datetime, cutoff_minutes: int) -> bool:
    """Return whether entries are allowed at this instant before the close cutoff."""
    instant = _normalize_utc(at_utc)
    if session_status(instant) is not SessionStatus.REGULAR:
        return False
    session = session_for(instant.astimezone(NEW_YORK).date())
    return instant < entry_cutoff(session, cutoff_minutes)


def next_session(after: date) -> Session:
    """Return the first session strictly after *after*."""
    if not isinstance(after, date) or isinstance(after, datetime):
        raise TypeError("after must be a datetime.date")
    _check_year(after)
    day = after + timedelta(days=1)
    while day.year <= SUPPORTED_YEAR_END:
        if _is_trading_day_unchecked(day):
            return session_for(day)
        day += timedelta(days=1)
    raise ValueError("no next session within supported year range")


def previous_session(before: date) -> Session:
    """Return the last session strictly before *before*."""
    if not isinstance(before, date) or isinstance(before, datetime):
        raise TypeError("before must be a datetime.date")
    _check_year(before)
    day = before - timedelta(days=1)
    while day.year >= SUPPORTED_YEAR_START:
        if _is_trading_day_unchecked(day):
            return session_for(day)
        day -= timedelta(days=1)
    raise ValueError("no previous session within supported year range")


__all__ = [
    "NEW_YORK",
    "SUPPORTED_YEAR_START",
    "SUPPORTED_YEAR_END",
    "SPECIAL_OVERRIDES",
    "Session",
    "SessionStatus",
    "is_trading_day",
    "session_for",
    "session_status",

"""Deterministic multi-timeframe intraday candle builders with closed-bar finalization.

Pure in-memory aggregation: no network, provider, or broker I/O, and no raw tick
archive.  Only bounded per-(symbol, timeframe) candle history is retained.

Design choices:
1. ``Candle`` here is a separate value type from ``mike_trade.domain.market.Candle``.
   The domain type has no DEVELOPING/CLOSED status, price basis, or origin, and its
   ``Timeframe`` enum has no 30m member, so this module carries its own
   ``CandleTimeframe`` (1m/5m/15m/30m/60m).  Numeric/UTC validation reuses the
   public helpers in ``mike_trade.domain.instruments``.
2. Inputs are ``TradeTick`` (trade ticks) or ``MinuteBar`` (completed 1-minute bars).
   Both build the 1m series; 5m/15m/30m/60m aggregate only from closed 1m candles.
3. Buckets are half-open ``[start, end)`` and aligned from an America/New_York anchor
   (midnight by default).  ``session_open`` is a plain ``datetime.time`` or a
   ``Callable[[date], time | None]`` so 60m buckets can start at e.g. 09:30 ET; the
   h.3 calendar module is not imported.
4. A bucket is closed once ``end <= horizon`` where ``horizon`` is the newest input
   timestamp seen for the symbol, or ``clock.now() - grace`` when a clock is injected.
   Closed candles are never mutated; a later event for a closed bucket is counted as
   late and dropped.  A 1m bar's timestamp is its start, so it closes earlier buckets
   but not its own.
5. The first accepted input locks the symbol's (feed_id, consolidated, price_basis);
   any later input that differs raises ``SeriesMismatchError`` before state changes.
"""

def _wrap[T](fn: Callable[[], T]) -> T:
    try:
        return fn()
    except InvalidCandleInputError:
        raise
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise InvalidCandleInputError(str(exc), code="invalid_candle_input") from exc


def _utc(value: datetime, field: str) -> datetime:
    return _wrap(lambda: require_utc(value, field=field))


def _positive(value: Decimal | int | str, field: str) -> Decimal:
    return _wrap(lambda: require_positive(value, field=field))


def _non_negative(value: Decimal | int | str, field: str) -> Decimal:
    return _wrap(lambda: require_non_negative(value, field=field))


def _invalid(message: str) -> InvalidCandleInputError:
    return InvalidCandleInputError(message, code="invalid_candle_input")


def _symbol(value: object) -> str:
    text = value.strip().upper() if isinstance(value, str) else ""
    if not text:
        raise _invalid("symbol must be a non-empty str")
    return text


def _provenance(
    feed_id: object, consolidated: object, price_basis: object
) -> tuple[str, bool, PriceBasis]:
    feed = feed_id.strip().lower() if isinstance(feed_id, str) else ""
    if not feed:
        raise _invalid("feed_id must be a non-empty str")
    if not isinstance(consolidated, bool):
        raise _invalid("consolidated must be bool")
    if feed == "iex" and consolidated:
        raise _invalid("IEX feed is not consolidated")
    if not isinstance(price_basis, PriceBasis):
        raise _invalid("price_basis must be PriceBasis")
    return feed, consolidated, price_basis


def _trade_count(value: object) -> int | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
        raise _invalid("trade_count must be a non-negative int or None")
    return value


def _check_ohlc(o: Decimal, h: Decimal, lo: Decimal, c: Decimal) -> None:
    if h < lo:
        raise _invalid(f"high ({h!s}) must be >= low ({lo!s})")
    if not lo <= o <= h:
        raise _invalid(f"open ({o!s}) must be within [low, high]")
    if not lo <= c <= h:
        raise _invalid(f"close ({c!s}) must be within [low, high]")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Candle:
    """One immutable OHLCV candle over the half-open UTC interval ``[start, end)``."""

    symbol: str
    timeframe: CandleTimeframe
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    open: Decimal  # noqa: A003 - OHLC field names
    high: Decimal
    low: Decimal
    close: Decimal
    volume: Decimal
    feed_id: str
    consolidated: bool
    origin: CandleOrigin
    price_basis: PriceBasis
    status: CandleStatus
    trade_count: int | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "symbol", _symbol(self.symbol))
        if not isinstance(self.timeframe, CandleTimeframe):
            raise _invalid("timeframe must be CandleTimeframe")
        start = _utc(self.start, "start")
        end = _utc(self.end, "end")
        if end != start + self.timeframe.duration:
            raise _invalid("end must equal start + timeframe duration")
        object.__setattr__(self, "start", start)
        object.__setattr__(self, "end", end)
        o = _positive(self.open, "open")
        h = _positive(self.high, "high")
        lo = _positive(self.low, "low")
        c = _positive(self.close, "close")
        _check_ohlc(o, h, lo, c)
        for name, val in (("open", o), ("high", h), ("low", lo), ("close", c)):
            object.__setattr__(self, name, val)
        object.__setattr__(self, "volume", _non_negative(self.volume, "volume"))
        feed, _, _ = _provenance(self.feed_id, self.consolidated, self.price_basis)
        object.__setattr__(self, "feed_id", feed)
        if not isinstance(self.origin, CandleOrigin):
            raise _invalid("origin must be CandleOrigin")
        if not isinstance(self.status, CandleStatus):
            raise _invalid("status must be CandleStatus")
        object.__setattr__(self, "trade_count", _trade_count(self.trade_count))

    @property
    def is_closed(self) -> bool:
        return self.status is CandleStatus.CLOSED

"""Immutable strategy market-context snapshots and the reference-symbol binder.

Pure in-memory assembly: no network, provider, or broker I/O, and no on-demand
fetching.  The builder only reads state already held by its injected sources (the
h.1 candle builder, the quote/trade cache, the h.3 calendar, and a clock).  It makes

1. ``MarketContext`` here is the strategy-facing snapshot keyed by
   ``(symbol, as_of, version)``; it is distinct from the older
   ``mike_trade.domain.market.MarketContext`` and reuses the h.1 ``Candle`` type.
2. ``candles`` holds CLOSED candles only (enforced by the value object).  A
   developing candle appears solely in ``developing_candles`` and only when the
   strategy declared ``completed_bars_only=False``.  Indicators are always computed
   from closed candles, never from the developing one.
3. Integrity fails closed: mixed ``(feed_id, consolidated)`` pairs, any non-RAW candle
   (stop-relevant prices are always RAW), a developing candle in ``candles``, or data
   timestamped after ``as_of`` raise ``ContextIntegrityError`` with a reason code.
4. Staleness is data age relative to ``as_of``; a stale context is still a valid value
   but is flagged, and :func:`select_context` never presents it as fresh.

class NyseCalendar:
    """Adapter over the module-level h.3 NYSE calendar functions."""

    def session_status(self, at_utc: datetime) -> SessionStatus:
        return _nyse.session_status(at_utc)

    def session_id(self, at_utc: datetime) -> str | None:
        """Session id of the trading day containing ``at_utc`` (ET), or None."""
        if _nyse.session_status(at_utc) is SessionStatus.UNKNOWN:
            return None
        day: date = at_utc.astimezone(_nyse.NEW_YORK).date()
        if not _nyse.is_trading_day(day):
            return None
        session: Session = _nyse.session_for(day)
        return session.session_id

"""Immutable strategy definitions, registrations, and evaluation results.

This module uses only the Python standard library.  In particular, it does
not import market, broker, account, order, or protection types at runtime.

Design choices (2 of 3 for these strategy/signal contracts):
1. Symbols are stripped and uppercased at the contract boundary, matching the
   normalization used by the rest of the domain while keeping strategy keys
   strictly lowercase snake_case.
2. Parameter mappings are defensively shallow-copied into ``MappingProxyType``;
   the contract makes the mapping itself read-only without prescribing or
   transforming strategy-specific parameter values.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass

_STRATEGY_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*$")


def _require_non_empty_str(value: object, *, field: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a non-empty str")
    return value.strip()


def _require_strategy_key(value: object, *, field: str) -> str:
    result = _require_non_empty_str(value, field=field)
    if _STRATEGY_KEY_RE.fullmatch(result) is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be lowercase snake_case; got {value!r}")
    return result


def _require_symbol(value: object, *, field: str) -> str:
    result = _require_non_empty_str(value, field=field).upper()
    if any(character.isspace() for character in result):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must not contain whitespace; got {value!r}")
    return result


def _require_utc(value: object, *, field: str) -> datetime:
    if not isinstance(value, datetime):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a datetime; got {type(value).__name__}")
    if value.tzinfo is None or value.utcoffset() is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be timezone-aware")
    return value.astimezone(UTC)


def _read_only_mapping(value: object, *, field: str) -> Mapping[str, object]:
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a mapping; got {type(value).__name__}")
    copied: dict[str, object] = {}
    for key, item in value.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError(f"{field} keys must be non-empty strings")
        copied[key] = item
    return MappingProxyType(copied)


def _string_tuple(value: object, *, field: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    if not isinstance(value, tuple):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a tuple")
    if any(not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip() for item in value):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} items must be non-empty strings")
    return tuple(item.strip() for item in value)

        object.__setattr__(self, "version", _require_non_empty_str(self.version, field="version"))
        if not isinstance(self.role, StrategyRole):
            raise ValueError(f"role must be StrategyRole; got {type(self.role).__name__}")
        if not isinstance(self.description, str):
            raise ValueError("description must be str")
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "required_timeframes",
            _string_tuple(self.required_timeframes, field="required_timeframes"),
        )
        if isinstance(self.warmup_bars, bool) or not isinstance(self.warmup_bars, int):
            raise ValueError("warmup_bars must be int")
        if self.warmup_bars < 0:
            raise ValueError("warmup_bars must be >= 0")
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "default_parameters",
            _read_only_mapping(self.default_parameters, field="default_parameters"),
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class StrategyInstance:
    """One configured BUY or SELL strategy registration."""

    instance_id: str
    strategy_key: str
    strategy_version: str
    role: StrategyRole
    symbol: str
    account_scope_id: str
    parameters: Mapping[str, object]
    enabled: bool
    pair_key: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(
            self, "instance_id", _require_non_empty_str(self.instance_id, field="instance_id")
        )
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "strategy_key",
            _require_strategy_key(self.strategy_key, field="strategy_key"),
        )
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "strategy_version",
            _require_non_empty_str(self.strategy_version, field="strategy_version"),
        )
        if not isinstance(self.role, StrategyRole):
            raise ValueError(f"role must be StrategyRole; got {type(self.role).__name__}")
        object.__setattr__(self, "symbol", _require_symbol(self.symbol, field="symbol"))
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "account_scope_id",
            _require_non_empty_str(self.account_scope_id, field="account_scope_id"),
        )
        object.__setattr__(
            self, "parameters", _read_only_mapping(self.parameters, field="parameters")
        )
        if not isinstance(self.enabled, bool):
            raise ValueError("enabled must be bool")
        if self.pair_key is not None:
            object.__setattr__(
                self, "pair_key", _require_non_empty_str(self.pair_key, field="pair_key")
            )


class EvaluationStatus(Enum):
    """The complete set of outcomes from one strategy evaluation."""

    NO_SIGNAL = "NO_SIGNAL"
    SIGNAL = "SIGNAL"
    INSUFFICIENT_DATA = "INSUFFICIENT_DATA"
    STALE_DATA = "STALE_DATA"
    ERROR = "ERROR"
    NOT_DUE = "NOT_DUE"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Evaluation:
    """The broker-neutral result of evaluating one strategy instance."""

    instance_id: str
    symbol: str
    evaluated_at: datetime
    bar_time: datetime | None
    status: EvaluationStatus
    signal: Signal | None
    reason: str
    error_detail: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        instance_id = _require_non_empty_str(self.instance_id, field="instance_id")
        symbol = _require_symbol(self.symbol, field="symbol")
        object.__setattr__(self, "instance_id", instance_id)
        object.__setattr__(self, "symbol", symbol)
        object.__setattr__(
            self, "evaluated_at", _require_utc(self.evaluated_at, field="evaluated_at")
        )
        if self.bar_time is not None:
            object.__setattr__(self, "bar_time", _require_utc(self.bar_time, field="bar_time"))
        if not isinstance(self.status, EvaluationStatus):
            raise ValueError(
                f"status must be EvaluationStatus; got {type(self.status).__name__}"
            )
        if not isinstance(self.reason, str):
            raise ValueError("reason must be str")
        if self.error_detail is not None and not isinstance(self.error_detail, str):
            raise ValueError("error_detail must be str or None")

        if self.status is EvaluationStatus.SIGNAL:
            if self.signal is None:
                raise ValueError("SIGNAL evaluations require a signal")
            if getattr(self.signal, "instance_id", None) != instance_id:
                raise ValueError("evaluation and signal instance_id must match")
            if getattr(self.signal, "symbol", None) != symbol:
                raise ValueError("evaluation and signal symbol must match")
        elif self.signal is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.status.value} evaluations must not contain a signal")

        if self.status is EvaluationStatus.ERROR and not self.error_detail:
            raise ValueError("ERROR evaluations require error_detail")

"""Immutable strategy definitions, registrations, and evaluation results.

This module uses only the Python standard library.  In particular, it does
not import market, broker, account, order, or protection types at runtime.

Design choices (2 of 3 for these strategy/signal contracts):
1. Symbols are stripped and uppercased at the contract boundary, matching the
   normalization used by the rest of the domain while keeping strategy keys
   strictly lowercase snake_case.
2. Parameter mappings are defensively shallow-copied into ``MappingProxyType``;
   the contract makes the mapping itself read-only without prescribing or
   transforming strategy-specific parameter values.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from enum import Enum
from types import MappingProxyType
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from mike_trade.domain.signals import Signal

__all__ = [
    "StrategyRole",
    "StrategyDefinition",
    "StrategyInstance",
    "EvaluationStatus",
    "Evaluation",
]

_STRATEGY_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*$")


def _require_non_empty_str(value: object, *, field: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a non-empty str")
    return value.strip()


def _require_strategy_key(value: object, *, field: str) -> str:
    result = _require_non_empty_str(value, field=field)
    if _STRATEGY_KEY_RE.fullmatch(result) is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be lowercase snake_case; got {value!r}")
    return result


def _require_symbol(value: object, *, field: str) -> str:
    result = _require_non_empty_str(value, field=field).upper()
    if any(character.isspace() for character in result):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must not contain whitespace; got {value!r}")
    return result


def _require_utc(value: object, *, field: str) -> datetime:
    if not isinstance(value, datetime):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a datetime; got {type(value).__name__}")
    if value.tzinfo is None or value.utcoffset() is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be timezone-aware")
    return value.astimezone(UTC)


def _read_only_mapping(value: object, *, field: str) -> Mapping[str, object]:
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a mapping; got {type(value).__name__}")
    copied: dict[str, object] = {}
    for key, item in value.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError(f"{field} keys must be non-empty strings")
        copied[key] = item
    return MappingProxyType(copied)


def _string_tuple(value: object, *, field: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    if not isinstance(value, tuple):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a tuple")
    if any(not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip() for item in value):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} items must be non-empty strings")
    return tuple(item.strip() for item in value)


class StrategyRole(Enum):
    """A strategy's independently registered entry or exit role."""

    BUY = "BUY"
    SELL = "SELL"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class StrategyDefinition:
    """Static metadata and defaults published by a strategy plugin."""

    strategy_key: str
    version: str
    role: StrategyRole
    description: str
    required_timeframes: tuple[str, ...]
    warmup_bars: int
    default_parameters: Mapping[str, object]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "strategy_key",
            _require_strategy_key(self.strategy_key, field="strategy_key"),
        )
        object.__setattr__(self, "version", _require_non_empty_str(self.version, field="version"))
        if not isinstance(self.role, StrategyRole):
            raise ValueError(f"role must be StrategyRole; got {type(self.role).__name__}")
        if not isinstance(self.description, str):
            raise ValueError("description must be str")
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "required_timeframes",
            _string_tuple(self.required_timeframes, field="required_timeframes"),
        )
        if isinstance(self.warmup_bars, bool) or not isinstance(self.warmup_bars, int):
            raise ValueError("warmup_bars must be int")
        if self.warmup_bars < 0:
            raise ValueError("warmup_bars must be >= 0")
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "default_parameters",
            _read_only_mapping(self.default_parameters, field="default_parameters"),
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class StrategyInstance:
    """One configured BUY or SELL strategy registration."""

    instance_id: str
    strategy_key: str
    strategy_version: str
    role: StrategyRole
    symbol: str
    account_scope_id: str
    parameters: Mapping[str, object]
    enabled: bool
    pair_key: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(
            self, "instance_id", _require_non_empty_str(self.instance_id, field="instance_id")
        )
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "strategy_key",
            _require_strategy_key(self.strategy_key, field="strategy_key"),
        )
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "strategy_version",
            _require_non_empty_str(self.strategy_version, field="strategy_version"),
        )
        if not isinstance(self.role, StrategyRole):
            raise ValueError(f"role must be StrategyRole; got {type(self.role).__name__}")
        object.__setattr__(self, "symbol", _require_symbol(self.symbol, field="symbol"))
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "account_scope_id",
            _require_non_empty_str(self.account_scope_id, field="account_scope_id"),
        )
        object.__setattr__(
            self, "parameters", _read_only_mapping(self.parameters, field="parameters")
        )
        if not isinstance(self.enabled, bool):
            raise ValueError("enabled must be bool")
        if self.pair_key is not None:
            object.__setattr__(
                self, "pair_key", _require_non_empty_str(self.pair_key, field="pair_key")
            )


class EvaluationStatus(Enum):
    """The complete set of outcomes from one strategy evaluation."""

    NO_SIGNAL = "NO_SIGNAL"
    SIGNAL = "SIGNAL"
    INSUFFICIENT_DATA = "INSUFFICIENT_DATA"
    STALE_DATA = "STALE_DATA"
    ERROR = "ERROR"
    NOT_DUE = "NOT_DUE"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Evaluation:
    """The broker-neutral result of evaluating one strategy instance."""

    instance_id: str
    symbol: str
    evaluated_at: datetime
    bar_time: datetime | None
    status: EvaluationStatus
    signal: Signal | None
    reason: str
    error_detail: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        instance_id = _require_non_empty_str(self.instance_id, field="instance_id")
        symbol = _require_symbol(self.symbol, field="symbol")
        object.__setattr__(self, "instance_id", instance_id)
        object.__setattr__(self, "symbol", symbol)
        object.__setattr__(
            self, "evaluated_at", _require_utc(self.evaluated_at, field="evaluated_at")
        )
        if self.bar_time is not None:
            object.__setattr__(self, "bar_time", _require_utc(self.bar_time, field="bar_time"))
        if not isinstance(self.status, EvaluationStatus):
            raise ValueError(
                f"status must be EvaluationStatus; got {type(self.status).__name__}"
            )
        if not isinstance(self.reason, str):
            raise ValueError("reason must be str")
        if self.error_detail is not None and not isinstance(self.error_detail, str):
            raise ValueError("error_detail must be str or None")

        if self.status is EvaluationStatus.SIGNAL:
            if self.signal is None:
                raise ValueError("SIGNAL evaluations require a signal")
            if getattr(self.signal, "instance_id", None) != instance_id:
                raise ValueError("evaluation and signal instance_id must match")
            if getattr(self.signal, "symbol", None) != symbol:
                raise ValueError("evaluation and signal symbol must match")
        elif self.signal is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.status.value} evaluations must not contain a signal")

        if self.status is EvaluationStatus.ERROR and not self.error_detail:
            raise ValueError("ERROR evaluations require error_detail")
"""
Runtime object graph, execution modes, and component ports.

The ports defined here are minimal, broker-neutral ``typing.Protocol`` types used only to type
the slots of :class:`Runtime`. Concrete implementations are wired in ``mike_trade.app``.
"""

import logging
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Protocol


class ExecutionMode(StrEnum):
    """Supported execution modes for mike_trade."""

    BACKTEST = "BACKTEST"
    SHADOW = "SHADOW"
    PAPER = "PAPER"
    LIVE = "LIVE"


class ClockPort(Protocol):
    """Time provider."""

    def now(self) -> datetime:
        """Returns the current timezone-aware UTC datetime."""
        ...


class SchedulerPort(Protocol):
    """Internal due-time scheduler."""

    def schedule(self, name: str, due: datetime) -> None:
        """Registers a named task to fire at a timezone-aware UTC time."""
        ...


class BrokerPort(Protocol):
    """Broker-neutral order gateway."""

    def submit_order(self, order: object) -> object:
        """Submits an order and returns the broker acknowledgement."""
        ...

    def cancel_order(self, order_id: str) -> None:
        """Requests cancellation of an open order."""
        ...


class MarketDataPort(Protocol):
    """Shared market-data service."""

    def subscribe(self, symbols: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Subscribes to market data for the given symbols."""
        ...


class ResearchPort(Protocol):
    """Optional offline research-data source."""

    def fetch_inputs(self, symbol: str) -> Mapping[str, object]:
        """Returns research inputs declared for the symbol."""
        ...


class PersistencePort(Protocol):
    """Authoritative append-only event journal."""

    def append_event(self, event: Mapping[str, object]) -> None:
        """Appends a trade-affecting event to the journal."""
        ...


class PortfolioPort(Protocol):
    """Position-cycle and account views."""

    def positions(self) -> Sequence[object]:
        """Returns the currently managed positions."""
        ...


class RiskPort(Protocol):
    """Entry-eligibility policy."""

    def check_entry(self, intent: object) -> None:
        """Raises ``EntryBlockedError`` when the entry intent is not eligible."""
        ...


class ExecutionPort(Protocol):
    """Provider-neutral order manager."""

    def submit_intent(self, intent: object) -> None:
        """Accepts an order intent for durable, serialized execution."""
        ...


class ReportingPort(Protocol):
    """Reporting and audit export."""

    def publish(self, report: Mapping[str, object]) -> None:
        """Publishes a report artifact."""
        ...


class ControlsPort(Protocol):
    """Operator control state."""

    def entries_enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Returns whether new entries are currently permitted."""
        ...


class SystemClock:
    """Default system clock providing timezone-aware UTC datetimes."""

    def now(self) -> datetime:
        return datetime.now(UTC)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Runtime:
    """Dependency-injected composition root container."""

    mode: ExecutionMode
    clock: ClockPort
    scheduler: SchedulerPort
    broker: BrokerPort
    market_data: MarketDataPort
    research: ResearchPort | None
    persistence: PersistencePort
    portfolio: PortfolioPort
    risk: RiskPort
    execution: ExecutionPort
    reporting: ReportingPort
    controls: ControlsPort
    logger: logging.Logger

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Lifecycle hook to start the runtime.

        Does not place orders, mutate positions, or contact a broker.
        """
        self.logger.info("Runtime started", extra={"mode": self.mode.value})

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Lifecycle hook to stop the runtime.

        Does not liquidate positions, cancel orders (including protective stops), or contact
        a broker.
        """
        self.logger.info("Runtime stopped", extra={"mode": self.mode.value})
"""Immutable strategy market-context snapshots and the reference-symbol binder.

Pure in-memory assembly: no network, provider, or broker I/O, and no on-demand
fetching.  The builder only reads state already held by its injected sources (the
h.1 candle builder, the quote/trade cache, the h.3 calendar, and a clock).  It makes
no BUY/SELL decisions.

Design choices:
1. ``MarketContext`` here is the strategy-facing snapshot keyed by
   ``(symbol, as_of, version)``; it is distinct from the older
   ``mike_trade.domain.market.MarketContext`` and reuses the h.1 ``Candle`` type.
2. ``candles`` holds CLOSED candles only (enforced by the value object).  A
   developing candle appears solely in ``developing_candles`` and only when the
   strategy declared ``completed_bars_only=False``.  Indicators are always computed
   from closed candles, never from the developing one.
3. Integrity fails closed: mixed ``(feed_id, consolidated)`` pairs, any non-RAW candle
   (stop-relevant prices are always RAW), a developing candle in ``candles``, or data
   timestamped after ``as_of`` raise ``ContextIntegrityError`` with a reason code.
4. Staleness is data age relative to ``as_of``; a stale context is still a valid value
   but is flagged, and :func:`select_context` never presents it as fresh.
5. The builder does not call ``CandleBuilder.close_due``; the owner of the candle
   builder drives bar closing, so a build never mutates a source.

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

def _decimal(value: object, field: str, *, positive: bool = True) -> Decimal:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (Decimal, int)):
        raise _invalid(f"{field} must be a Decimal or int")
    result = Decimal(value)
    if not result.is_finite() or (result <= 0 if positive else result < 0):
        raise _invalid(f"{field} must be finite and {'positive' if positive else 'non-negative'}")
    return result

class NyseCalendar:
    """Adapter over the module-level h.3 NYSE calendar functions."""

    def session_status(self, at_utc: datetime) -> SessionStatus:
        return _nyse.session_status(at_utc)

    def session_id(self, at_utc: datetime) -> str | None:
        """Session id of the trading day containing ``at_utc`` (ET), or None."""
        if _nyse.session_status(at_utc) is SessionStatus.UNKNOWN:
            return None
        day: date = at_utc.astimezone(_nyse.NEW_YORK).date()

def _quote_snapshot(update: MarketDataUpdate, symbol: str) -> QuoteSnapshot:
    if update.kind != "quote" or update.symbol != symbol:
        raise _invalid(f"cache returned a non-quote or foreign-symbol update for {symbol}")
    return QuoteSnapshot(
        symbol=symbol,
        bid=update.bid,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        ask=update.ask,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        bid_size=_optional_size(update.get("bid_size")),
        ask_size=_optional_size(update.get("ask_size")),
        provider_ts=update.provider_source_ts,
        receive_ts=update.receive_ts,
        feed_id=update.feed_id,
    )


def _trade_snapshot(update: MarketDataUpdate, symbol: str) -> TradeSnapshot:
    if update.kind != "trade" or update.symbol != symbol:
        raise _invalid(f"cache returned a non-trade or foreign-symbol update for {symbol}")
    return TradeSnapshot(
        symbol=symbol,
        price=update.price,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        size=_optional_size(update.get("size")),
        provider_ts=update.provider_source_ts,
        receive_ts=update.receive_ts,
        feed_id=update.feed_id,
    )


def _optional_size(value: object) -> Decimal | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, float):  # sizes from some providers arrive as floats
        value = Decimal(str(value))
    return _decimal(value, "size", positive=False)

class ContextFreshness:

        if self.newest_data_ts is not None:

        if (self.newest_data_ts is None) != (self.age is None):
            raise _invalid("newest_data_ts and age must both be set or both be None")
        if self.age is not None and (not isinstance(self.age, timedelta) or self.age < _ZERO):
            raise _invalid("age must be a non-negative timedelta")
        if not isinstance(self.max_age, timedelta) or self.max_age <= _ZERO:

        if not isinstance(self.stale, bool):

        if self.stale and not (isinstance(self.reason, str) and self.reason):
            raise _invalid("stale freshness requires a reason code")
        if not self.stale and self.reason is not None:
            raise _invalid("fresh freshness must not carry a reason")

The module deliberately depends only on the Python standard library.

Design choices (3 of the task's 4-decision budget):
1. Symbols are stripped and uppercased at construction, while opaque IDs are

2. A cycle's realized P&L is the literal exit proceeds minus total entry cost

3. ``entry_blocked`` returns stored reasons and adds the stable reason

def _require_text(value: object, *, field: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a non-empty str")
    return value.strip()


def _require_symbol(value: object) -> str:
    symbol = _require_text(value, field="symbol").upper()
    if any(character.isspace() for character in symbol):
        raise ValueError("symbol must not contain whitespace")
    return symbol


def _require_decimal(
    value: object,
    *,
    field: str,
    minimum: Decimal = _ZERO,
    inclusive: bool = True,
) -> Decimal:
    if not isinstance(value, Decimal):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be Decimal; got {type(value).__name__}")
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be finite")
    if value < minimum or (not inclusive and value == minimum):
        operator = ">=" if inclusive else ">"
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be {operator} {minimum}")
    return value


def _optional_decimal(
    value: object,
    *,
    field: str,
    minimum: Decimal = _ZERO,
    inclusive: bool = True,
) -> Decimal | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    return _require_decimal(value, field=field, minimum=minimum, inclusive=inclusive)


def _require_utc(value: object, *, field: str) -> datetime:
    if not isinstance(value, datetime):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a datetime")
    if value.tzinfo is None or value.utcoffset() is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be timezone-aware UTC")
    if value.utcoffset() != timedelta(0):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be UTC")
    return value.astimezone(UTC)


def _optional_utc(value: object, *, field: str) -> datetime | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    return _require_utc(value, field=field)


def _require_enum(value: object, enum_type: type[Enum], *, field: str) -> None:
    if not isinstance(value, enum_type):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be {enum_type.__name__}")


def _require_int(value: object, *, field: str, minimum: int) -> int:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be int")
    if value < minimum:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be >= {minimum}")
    return value


def _require_duration(value: object, *, field: str) -> timedelta:
    if not isinstance(value, timedelta):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be timedelta")
    if value < timedelta(0):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be >= 0")
    return value


def _validate_order_prices(
    order_type: OrderType,
    limit_price: Decimal | None,
    stop_price: Decimal | None,
    trail_price: Decimal | None,
    trail_percent: Decimal | None,
) -> None:
    if order_type in {OrderType.LIMIT, OrderType.STOP_LIMIT}:
        if limit_price is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{order_type.value} orders require limit_price")
    elif limit_price is not None:
        raise ValueError(f"{order_type.value} orders must not specify limit_price")

    if order_type in {OrderType.STOP, OrderType.STOP_LIMIT}:
        if stop_price is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{order_type.value} orders require stop_price")
    elif stop_price is not None:
        raise ValueError(f"{order_type.value} orders must not specify stop_price")

    if order_type is OrderType.TRAILING_STOP:
        if trail_count != 1:
            raise ValueError("TRAILING_STOP orders require exactly one trail value")
    elif trail_count:
        raise ValueError(f"{order_type.value} orders must not specify a trail value")

+QUOTE_CHANGE: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.QUOTE_CHANGE)
+SESSION_OPEN: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.SESSION_OPEN)
+ENTRY_CUTOFF: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.ENTRY_CUTOFF)
+SESSION_CLOSE: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.SESSION_CLOSE)
+MANUAL: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.MANUAL)

+
+    return StrategyTrigger.candle_closed(timeframe)
+
+
+def INTERVAL(seconds: float | int) -> StrategyTrigger:
+    """Build a positive elapsed-time declaration."""
+
+    return StrategyTrigger.interval(seconds)

+            raise ValueError(f"{kind.value} is not a session trigger")
+        object.__setattr__(self, "kind", kind)
+        object.__setattr__(self, "session_id", _identifier(self.session_id, "session_id"))
+        object.__setattr__(self, "due_at", _utc(self.due_at, "due_at"))
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ControlTick:
+    """Request a cadence check using the scheduler's injected clock."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ManualEvaluationRequest:
+    symbol: str
+    strategy_id: str
+    side: StrategyRole | str
+    request_id: str | None = None
+    due_at: datetime | None = None
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        object.__setattr__(self, "symbol", _symbol(self.symbol))
+        object.__setattr__(self, "strategy_id", _identifier(self.strategy_id, "strategy_id"))
+        object.__setattr__(self, "side", _side(self.side))
+        if self.request_id is not None:
+            object.__setattr__(self, "request_id", _identifier(self.request_id, "request_id"))
+        if self.due_at is not None:
+            object.__setattr__(self, "due_at", _utc(self.due_at, "due_at"))
+
+
+SchedulingEvent: TypeAlias = (
+    MarketDataArrivalEvent
+    | QuoteChangeEvent
+    | CandleClosedEvent
+    | SessionEvent
+    | ControlTick
+    | ManualEvaluationRequest
+)
+
+
+class _DefaultCalendar:
+    def session_for(self, day: date) -> Session:
+        return exchange_calendar.session_for(day)
+
+    def entry_cutoff(self, session: Session, minutes_before_close: int) -> datetime:
+        return exchange_calendar.entry_cutoff(session, minutes_before_close)
+
+
+_PRIORITY = {
+    TriggerKind.SESSION_OPEN: 0,
+    TriggerKind.ENTRY_CUTOFF: 0,
+    TriggerKind.SESSION_CLOSE: 0,
+    TriggerKind.CANDLE_CLOSED: 1,
+    TriggerKind.QUOTE_CHANGE: 2,
+    TriggerKind.MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL: 2,
+    TriggerKind.INTERVAL: 3,
+    TriggerKind.MANUAL: 4,
+}
+
+_RegistryKey = tuple[str, str, StrategyRole]
+_SeenKey = tuple[_RegistryKey, TriggerKind, object]
+
+
+class StrategyScheduler:
+    """One deterministic scheduler shared by every symbol and strategy.
+
+    The synchronous :meth:`process` API is useful to an engine event loop that
+    already serializes inputs.  :meth:`handle` provides an asyncio-safe entry
+    point using one scheduler-level lock; neither API creates background tasks.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        clock: ClockLike,
+        *,
+        calendar: CalendarLike | None = None,
+        watched_symbols: Iterable[str] = (),
+        entry_cutoff_minutes: int = 30,
+    ) -> None:
+        if not hasattr(clock, "now"):
+            raise TypeError("clock must provide now()")
+        if (
+            isinstance(entry_cutoff_minutes, bool)
+            or not isinstance(entry_cutoff_minutes, int)
+            or entry_cutoff_minutes < 0
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("entry_cutoff_minutes must be a non-negative integer")
+        self._clock = clock
+        self._calendar: CalendarLike = calendar or _DefaultCalendar()
+        self._entry_cutoff_minutes = entry_cutoff_minutes
+        self._watched = {_symbol(symbol) for symbol in watched_symbols}
+        self._registry: dict[_RegistryKey, StrategySchedule] = {}
+        self._registered_at: dict[_RegistryKey, datetime] = {}
+        self._next_interval: dict[tuple[_RegistryKey, StrategyTrigger], datetime] = {}
+        self._latest_snapshot: dict[str, int] = {}
+        self._quotes: dict[str, tuple[Decimal, Decimal]] = {}
+        self._seen: set[_SeenKey] = set()
+        self._last_control_at = self._now()
+        self._manual_sequence = 0
+        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()
+
+    def _now(self) -> datetime:
+        return _utc(self._clock.now(), "clock.now()")
+
+    @property
+    def watched_symbols(self) -> frozenset[str]:
+        return frozenset(self._watched)
+
+    @property
+    def registrations(self) -> tuple[StrategySchedule, ...]:
+        return tuple(sorted(self._registry.values(), key=self._registration_sort_key))
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _registration_sort_key(item: StrategySchedule) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
+        return item.symbol, item.strategy_id, item.side.value
+
+    def watch(self, symbol: str) -> None:
+        self._watched.add(_symbol(symbol))
+
+    watch_symbol = watch
+
+    def unwatch(self, symbol: str) -> None:
+        self._watched.discard(_symbol(symbol))
+
+    unwatch_symbol = unwatch
+
+    def register(
+        self,
+        schedule: StrategySchedule | None = None,
+        *,
+        symbol: str | None = None,
+        strategy_id: str | None = None,
+        side: StrategyRole | str | None = None,
+        triggers: Iterable[StrategyTrigger] | None = None,
+        enabled: bool = True,
+        paused: bool = False,
+    ) -> StrategySchedule:
+        if schedule is None:
+            if symbol is None or strategy_id is None or side is None or triggers is None:
+                raise TypeError("register requires a schedule or symbol/strategy_id/side/triggers")
+            schedule = StrategySchedule(
+                symbol=symbol,
+                strategy_id=strategy_id,
+                side=side,
+                triggers=triggers,
+                enabled=enabled,
+                paused=paused,
+            )
+        elif any(value is not None for value in (symbol, strategy_id, side, triggers)):
+            raise TypeError("schedule cannot be combined with registration fields")
+        elif not isinstance(schedule, StrategySchedule):
+            raise TypeError("schedule must be StrategySchedule")
+
+        key = (schedule.symbol, schedule.strategy_id, schedule.side)
+        now = self._now()
+        self._registry[key] = schedule
+        self._registered_at[key] = now
+        for interval_key in tuple(self._next_interval):
+            if interval_key[0] == key:
+                del self._next_interval[interval_key]
+        for trigger in schedule.triggers:
+            if trigger.kind is TriggerKind.INTERVAL:
+                self._next_interval[(key, trigger)] = now + timedelta(
+                    seconds=trigger.interval_seconds  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+                )
+        return schedule
+
+    register_strategy = register
+
+    def unregister(self, symbol: str, strategy_id: str, side: StrategyRole | str) -> None:
+        key = (_symbol(symbol), _identifier(strategy_id, "strategy_id"), _side(side))
+        self._registry.pop(key, None)
+        self._registered_at.pop(key, None)
+        for interval_key in tuple(self._next_interval):
+            if interval_key[0] == key:
+                del self._next_interval[interval_key]
+
+    def set_state(
+        self,
+        symbol: str,
+        strategy_id: str,
+        side: StrategyRole | str,
+        *,
+        enabled: bool | None = None,
+        paused: bool | None = None,
+    ) -> StrategySchedule:
+        key = (_symbol(symbol), _identifier(strategy_id, "strategy_id"), _side(side))
+        current = self._registry[key]
+        if enabled is not None and not isinstance(enabled, bool):
+            raise ValueError("enabled must be bool")
+        if paused is not None and not isinstance(paused, bool):
+            raise ValueError("paused must be bool")
+        updated = replace(
+            current,
+            enabled=current.enabled if enabled is None else enabled,
+            paused=current.paused if paused is None else paused,
+        )
+        self._registry[key] = updated
+        return updated
+
+    def process(self, event: SchedulingEvent) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        """Process one input and return a deterministically ordered due list."""
+
+        return self.process_many((event,))
+
+    def process_many(self, events: Iterable[SchedulingEvent]) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        """Process inputs in their given order, then order all resulting records."""
+
+        due: list[DueEvaluation] = []
+        for event in events:
+            due.extend(self._process_one(event))
+        due.sort(key=self.sort_key)
+        return due
+
+    async def handle(self, event: SchedulingEvent) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        """Asyncio-safe event entry point using one component-wide lock."""
+
+        async with self._lock:
+            return self.process(event)
+
+    async def handle_many(self, events: Iterable[SchedulingEvent]) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        async with self._lock:
+            return self.process_many(events)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def sort_key(item: DueEvaluation) -> tuple[datetime, int, str, str, str]:
+        return (
+            item.due_at,
+            _PRIORITY[item.trigger_kind],
+            item.symbol,
+            item.strategy_id,
+            item.side.value,
+        )
+
+    def _process_one(self, event: SchedulingEvent) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        if isinstance(event, MarketDataArrivalEvent):
+            self._latest_snapshot[event.symbol] = event.snapshot_version
+            return self._emit_for_kind(
+                event.symbol,
+                TriggerKind.MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL,
+                event.due_at or self._now(),
+                snapshot_version=event.snapshot_version,
+                discriminator=event.snapshot_version,
+            )
+        if isinstance(event, QuoteChangeEvent):
+            self._latest_snapshot[event.symbol] = event.snapshot_version
+            quote = (event.bid, event.ask)
+            previous = self._quotes.get(event.symbol)
+            self._quotes[event.symbol] = quote
+            if quote == previous:
+                return []
+            return self._emit_for_kind(
+                event.symbol,
+                TriggerKind.QUOTE_CHANGE,
+                event.due_at or self._now(),
+                snapshot_version=event.snapshot_version,
+                discriminator=event.snapshot_version,
+            )
+        if isinstance(event, CandleClosedEvent):
+            if event.snapshot_version is not None:
+                self._latest_snapshot[event.symbol] = event.snapshot_version
+            bar_key = BarKey(event.symbol, event.timeframe, event.bar_end_utc)
+            return self._emit_for_kind(
+                event.symbol,
+                TriggerKind.CANDLE_CLOSED,
+                event.due_at or event.bar_end_utc,
+                snapshot_version=event.snapshot_version
+                if event.snapshot_version is not None
+                else self._latest_snapshot.get(event.symbol),
+                bar_key=bar_key,
+                discriminator=bar_key,
+                timeframe=event.timeframe,
+            )
+        if isinstance(event, SessionEvent):
+            return self._emit_all_symbols(
+                event.kind,
+                event.due_at,
+                discriminator=event.session_id,
+            )
+        if isinstance(event, ControlTick):
+            return self._control_tick()
+        if isinstance(event, ManualEvaluationRequest):
+            return self._manual(event)
+        raise TypeError(f"unsupported scheduling event {type(event).__name__}")
+
+    def _eligible(self, schedule: StrategySchedule) -> bool:
+        return (
+            schedule.symbol in self._watched and schedule.enabled and not schedule.paused
+        )
+
+    def _emit_for_kind(
+        self,
+        symbol: str,
+        kind: TriggerKind,
+        due_at: datetime,
+        *,
+        discriminator: object,
+        snapshot_version: int | None = None,
+        bar_key: BarKey | None = None,
+        timeframe: CandleTimeframe | None = None,
+    ) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        due: list[DueEvaluation] = []
+        for key, schedule in sorted(
+            self._registry.items(), key=lambda item: self._registration_sort_key(item[1])
+        ):
+            if schedule.symbol != symbol or not self._eligible(schedule):
+                continue
+            matching = [trigger for trigger in schedule.triggers if trigger.kind is kind]
+            if timeframe is not None:
+                matching = [trigger for trigger in matching if trigger.timeframe is timeframe]
+            if not matching:
+                continue
+            seen_key = (key, kind, discriminator)
+            if seen_key in self._seen:
+                continue
+            self._seen.add(seen_key)
+            due.append(
+                DueEvaluation(
+                    symbol=schedule.symbol,
+                    strategy_id=schedule.strategy_id,
+                    side=schedule.side,
+                    trigger_kind=kind,
+                    snapshot_version=snapshot_version,
+                    bar_key=bar_key,
+                    due_at=due_at,
+                )
+            )
+        return due
+
+    def _emit_all_symbols(
+        self, kind: TriggerKind, due_at: datetime, *, discriminator: object
+    ) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        due: list[DueEvaluation] = []
+        for symbol in sorted(self._watched):
+            due.extend(
+                self._emit_for_kind(
+                    symbol,
+                    kind,
+                    due_at,
+                    discriminator=discriminator,
+                    snapshot_version=self._latest_snapshot.get(symbol),
+                )
+            )
+        return due
+
+    def _manual(self, event: ManualEvaluationRequest) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        key = (event.symbol, event.strategy_id, event.side)
+        schedule = self._registry.get(key)
+        if (
+            schedule is None
+            or not self._eligible(schedule)
+            or all(trigger.kind is not TriggerKind.MANUAL for trigger in schedule.triggers)
+        ):
+            return []
+        self._manual_sequence += 1
+        discriminator: object = event.request_id or self._manual_sequence
+        seen_key = (key, TriggerKind.MANUAL, discriminator)
+        if seen_key in self._seen:
+            return []
+        self._seen.add(seen_key)
+        return [
+            DueEvaluation(
+                symbol=schedule.symbol,
+                strategy_id=schedule.strategy_id,
+                side=schedule.side,
+                trigger_kind=TriggerKind.MANUAL,
+                snapshot_version=self._latest_snapshot.get(schedule.symbol),
+                bar_key=None,
+                due_at=event.due_at or self._now(),
+            )
+        ]
+
+    def _control_tick(self) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        now = self._now()
+        if now < self._last_control_at:
+            raise ValueError("clock moved backwards")
+        due = self._session_boundaries(self._last_control_at, now)
+        due.extend(self._intervals(now))
+        self._last_control_at = now
+        return due
+
+    def _intervals(self, now: datetime) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        due: list[DueEvaluation] = []
+        for (key, trigger), next_due in sorted(
+            self._next_interval.items(),
+            key=lambda item: (
+                item[1],
+                item[0][0][0],
+                item[0][0][1],
+                item[0][0][2].value,
+                item[0][1].interval_seconds or 0,
+            ),
+        ):
+            schedule = self._registry.get(key)
+            if schedule is None or now < next_due:
+                continue
+            seconds = trigger.interval_seconds
+            assert seconds is not None
+            interval = timedelta(seconds=seconds)
+            elapsed = (now - next_due) // interval
+            self._next_interval[(key, trigger)] = next_due + interval * (elapsed + 1)
+            if not self._eligible(schedule):
+                continue
+            discriminator = next_due
+            seen_key = (key, TriggerKind.INTERVAL, discriminator)
+            if seen_key in self._seen:
+                continue
+            self._seen.add(seen_key)
+            due.append(
+                DueEvaluation(
+                    symbol=schedule.symbol,
+                    strategy_id=schedule.strategy_id,
+                    side=schedule.side,
+                    trigger_kind=TriggerKind.INTERVAL,
+                    snapshot_version=self._latest_snapshot.get(schedule.symbol),
+                    bar_key=None,
+                    due_at=next_due,
+                )
+            )
+        return due
+
+    def _session_boundaries(self, start: datetime, end: datetime) -> list[DueEvaluation]:
+        if end == start:
+            return []
+        due: list[DueEvaluation] = []
+        local_start = start.astimezone(exchange_calendar.NEW_YORK).date()
+        local_end = end.astimezone(exchange_calendar.NEW_YORK).date()
+        day = local_start
+        while day <= local_end:
+            try:
+                session = self._calendar.session_for(day)
+            except ValueError:
+                day += timedelta(days=1)
+                continue
+            cutoff = _utc(
+                self._calendar.entry_cutoff(session, self._entry_cutoff_minutes),
+                "entry cutoff",
+            )
+            boundaries = (
+                (TriggerKind.SESSION_OPEN, _utc(session.open_utc, "session open")),
+                (TriggerKind.ENTRY_CUTOFF, cutoff),
+                (TriggerKind.SESSION_CLOSE, _utc(session.close_utc, "session close")),
+            )
+            for kind, instant in boundaries:
+                if start < instant <= end:
+                    due.extend(
+                        self._emit_all_symbols(
+                            kind, instant, discriminator=session.session_id
+                        )
+                    )
+            day += timedelta(days=1)
+        return due
+
+
+# Alternate descriptive name for callers that do not use the Strategy prefix.
+DueScheduler = StrategyScheduler

+"""Declarative, immutable strategy scheduling triggers.
+
+The declarations in this module contain configuration only.  They deliberately
+have no references to strategies, market-data providers, or execution services.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import StrEnum
+from math import isfinite
+from typing import Final
+
+from mike_trade.domain.errors import ConfigurationError
+from mike_trade.market_data.candles import CandleTimeframe
+
+__all__ = [
+    "TriggerConfigurationError",
+    "TriggerKind",
+    "StrategyTrigger",
+    "Trigger",
+    "MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL",
+    "QUOTE_CHANGE",
+    "SESSION_OPEN",
+    "ENTRY_CUTOFF",
+    "SESSION_CLOSE",
+    "MANUAL",
+    "CANDLE_CLOSED",
+    "INTERVAL",
+]
+
+
+class TriggerConfigurationError(ConfigurationError, ValueError):
+    """Raised when a declarative trigger cannot be loaded safely."""
+
+
+class TriggerKind(StrEnum):
+    """The complete set of scheduler trigger kinds."""
+
+    MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL = "MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL"
+    QUOTE_CHANGE = "QUOTE_CHANGE"
+    CANDLE_CLOSED = "CANDLE_CLOSED"
+    INTERVAL = "INTERVAL"
+    SESSION_OPEN = "SESSION_OPEN"
+    ENTRY_CUTOFF = "ENTRY_CUTOFF"
+    SESSION_CLOSE = "SESSION_CLOSE"
+    MANUAL = "MANUAL"
+
+
+def _error(message: str) -> TriggerConfigurationError:
+    return TriggerConfigurationError(message, code="invalid_strategy_trigger")
+
+
+def _kind(value: object) -> TriggerKind:
+    if isinstance(value, TriggerKind):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        try:
+            return TriggerKind(value.strip().upper())
+        except ValueError:
+            pass
+    raise _error(f"unknown trigger kind {value!r}")
+
+
+def _timeframe(value: object) -> CandleTimeframe:
+    if isinstance(value, CandleTimeframe):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        try:
+            return CandleTimeframe(value.strip().lower())
+        except ValueError:
+            pass
+    supported = ", ".join(frame.value for frame in CandleTimeframe)
+    raise _error(f"unsupported candle timeframe {value!r}; expected one of {supported}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class StrategyTrigger:
+    """One validated trigger attached to a BUY or SELL strategy declaration.
+
+    ``timeframe`` is present only for :attr:`TriggerKind.CANDLE_CLOSED`, and
+    ``interval_seconds`` only for :attr:`TriggerKind.INTERVAL`.
+    """
+
+    kind: TriggerKind | str
+    timeframe: CandleTimeframe | str | None = None
+    interval_seconds: float | int | None = None
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        kind = _kind(self.kind)
+        object.__setattr__(self, "kind", kind)
+
+        if kind is TriggerKind.CANDLE_CLOSED:
+            if self.timeframe is None:
+                raise _error("CANDLE_CLOSED requires a supported timeframe")
+            object.__setattr__(self, "timeframe", _timeframe(self.timeframe))
+        elif self.timeframe is not None:
+            raise _error(f"{kind.value} must not specify a timeframe")
+
+        if kind is TriggerKind.INTERVAL:
+            seconds = self.interval_seconds
+            if (
+                isinstance(seconds, bool)
+                or not isinstance(seconds, (int, float))
+                or not isfinite(seconds)
+                or seconds <= 0
+            ):
+                raise _error("INTERVAL requires positive finite interval_seconds")
+            object.__setattr__(self, "interval_seconds", float(seconds))
+        elif self.interval_seconds is not None:
+            raise _error(f"{kind.value} must not specify interval_seconds")
+
+    @classmethod
+    def candle_closed(cls, timeframe: CandleTimeframe | str) -> StrategyTrigger:
+        return cls(TriggerKind.CANDLE_CLOSED, timeframe=timeframe)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def interval(cls, seconds: float | int) -> StrategyTrigger:
+        return cls(TriggerKind.INTERVAL, interval_seconds=seconds)
+
+
+# A short alias is convenient in strategy class configuration.
+Trigger = StrategyTrigger
+
+# Parameter-free declarations are safe to share because they are frozen values.
+MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.MARKET_DATA_ARRIVAL)
+QUOTE_CHANGE: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.QUOTE_CHANGE)
+SESSION_OPEN: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.SESSION_OPEN)
+ENTRY_CUTOFF: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.ENTRY_CUTOFF)
+SESSION_CLOSE: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.SESSION_CLOSE)
+MANUAL: Final = StrategyTrigger(TriggerKind.MANUAL)
+
+
+def CANDLE_CLOSED(timeframe: CandleTimeframe | str) -> StrategyTrigger:
+    """Build a closed-candle declaration for an h.1-supported timeframe."""
+
+    return StrategyTrigger.candle_closed(timeframe)
+
+
+def INTERVAL(seconds: float | int) -> StrategyTrigger:
+    """Build a positive elapsed-time declaration."""
+
+    return StrategyTrigger.interval(seconds)
